subject: Opportunity intake: align next steps for reserved pool sizing
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@finverse.com>
Cc: Finverse Ops <ops@finverse.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up + next step: dedicated capacity sizing call

Hi Jake — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can lock scope for a reserved GPU pool:

Summary:
- Primary workload: real-time fraud scoring + account summarization (batch embedding generation nightly).
- Expected peak concurrency: ~180 concurrent requests during peak windows.
- Typical prompt length: 80–250 tokens; avg response size 120 tokens.
- Initial latency target: 95th percentile <= 220ms for inference; acceptable fallback path at 350ms.

What we need next:
1) A dedicated capacity sizing call (technical deep dive) to confirm throughput targets, sequence distribution, KV cache patterns, and any retention/telemetry constraints.
2) Fill the attached intake form so our infra team has baseline traffic metrics before the call.

Proposed slots (PT):
- Tue 2028-11-14 10:00–10:45
- Wed 2028-11-15 13:00–13:45
- Thu 2028-11-16 09:30–10:15

If none of those work, send times that do and I will coordinate. I’m looping in Ben (solutions) and Naomi (inference eng) on the sizing call — they’ll run the technical deep dive and validate kernel/quantization recommendations.

Attachments: finverse_intake_form.pdf (short answers), mutual_action_plan.xlsx (draft)

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
[evelyn.hart@redwood.com] | +1 415-555-0198

---
Note: On the call you mentioned a compliance constraint around data retention. If that’s accurate, please flag which datasets need to be excluded from caching ahead of the technical deep dive.

From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@finverse.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Finverse Ops <ops@finverse.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Nov 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up + next step: dedicated capacity sizing call

Hi Evelyn — appreciate the clear recap. Confirming the workload description; a couple clarifications:
- Peak concurrency: closer to 200 burst for advertising windows (short spikes ~2–3 min).
- Nightly batch embedding job: ~6M items, but can be staged over 8 hours.
- Retention: PII must not be cached; we can provide scrubbed examples.

Of your proposed times, Wed 11/15 at 13:00 PT works best for our devs (I’ll be on the call, ops will join for retention talk). I’ve attached a short CSV with recent qps/latency snapshots.

Attachment: finverse_qps_snapshot.csv

—Jake
Jake Turner

Thanks — confirmed on my calendar for Wed 11/15 13:00 PT. Naomi and I did a quick pass on the snapshot Jake sent. Initial notes:
- We’ll model for 200 QPS bursts and a sustained 60–80 QPS baseline; need to validate whether bursts are vertical (all users at once) or per-route.
- Cache exclusions for PII are straightforward; please flag which endpoints return user-identifying tokens.
- For the batch embedding job, staging over 8 hours fits a reserve with non-preemptible GPUs; suggest a brief runbook item for throttling the job if on-peak spike occurs.

I attached a short checklist we’ll use in the sizing call (mutual_action_plan.xlsx). Also dropping the pre-call checklist link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/finverse-intake-form

If Finverse can return the intake form by Tue EOD, we’ll have an initial sizing draft to share during the call. Looking forward to it.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
[ben.carter@redwood.com] | +1 415-555-0123
